findings.summary: U8's acceptance criterion — 'repo-wide grep for the metaphor is empty outside historical/supersession text that names it as retired' — does not hold at the tip. 27 live occurrences of 'brick' and 4 of 'door'/'doorways' survive as snake_case and SCREAMING_SNAKE identifiers in seven tracked test files, plus 12 derived entries in tests/serial_compat_manifest.json. Same grep for 'door': tests/test_registry_census.py:161 (test_the_outline_and_slice_doorways_collapse_to_one_remedy), tests/test_ticket_frames.py:187 (test_a_wave_appends_through_the_result_door_under_the_frames_identity), tests/serial_compat_manifest.json:727,1017. Confirmed present already at the post-U8 merge 8187585d, so this is U8's own residue and not a later regression: git grep -icI "brick\|door" 8187585d -- tests/ returns the same seven files.
findings.cause: B1.8's own acceptance grep, quoted verbatim in its ## Report, was grep -rniIE "\b(bricks?|doors?|doorways?)\b". In POSIX and PCRE alike '_' is a word character, so \b never matches at '_brick', '_BRICK', '_door' or '_doorways'. The regex is structurally blind to exactly the place most of the residue lives — identifiers — which is why B1.8 reported 'tests/ grep is now empty' in good faith. The lawful-historical carve-out the driver accepted is NOT what let this through: every carve-out site is genuinely frozen text (verified independently under 'deviations' below).
findings.remedy: One mechanical follow-up commit renaming the identifiers (brick -> callable, door/doorway -> command/entry point, matching U8's own published mapping), then tools/run_serial_compat.py --write-manifest to carry the twelve derived manifest entries. Re-run the acceptance grep as a substring grep, not a word-boundary one. One scope decision for the driver: tests/test_browser_game_composition.py:60 tests a workflow the spec's Deferred list names as untouched migration debt, so it is arguably out of U8's surface — decide, do not leave it undecided.

Meanwhile git grep -nI "resolve().parents\[" HEAD -- scripts/ tools/ installer/ returns 31 sites, including tools/validate_support/common.py:13 ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] — the very module U5 made the owner of every terseness number. scripts/_bootstrap.py's own docstring calls these 'the two facts a caller must know', and ROOT's inline comment calls it 'the fact every independent Path(__file__).resolve().parent... chain elsewhere re-derives'.

findings.seam: U2 (conditional launch clauses) — a widening beyond the spec's named else-branch
findings.summary: U2's condition keys off workspace_strategy == 'git', which sweeps in the document-tree adapter the spec did not name. A content-pack child now receives no commit instruction while working uncommitted, without isolation, inside a git repository.
findings.evidence: scripts/tickets_assignment.py:201 git_candidate(pack) resolves True only for workspace_strategy == 'git'. scripts/tickets_adapters.py declares document-tree with establishes_isolation=False and workspace_strategy='document-tree'; :235 resolves its isolation to 'none'. Rendered live through tickets_assignment._craft: orch-content-pack -> git_candidate=False -> the prompt emits 'Your stamped pack commits nothing; its workspace channel is: "document tree: identities are document revisions; integration compares actual candidate changes and resolves section overlap."' The spec's U2(a) says 'Emit the commit clause only when the adapter establishes a git candidate; for evidence-store/derived-none adapters emit the pack's own workspace channel line instead' — document-tree is neither of the two named.
findings.cause: The spec's governing sentence and its else-branch enumeration disagree about one adapter, and U2 followed the governing sentence. U2's own stated acceptance names only the research-pack and code-pack cases, both of which I verified hold, so nothing in the unit's checks could surface the third case.
findings.remedy: This run's own history is the exposure: B1.1 was a content-pack child working in the run tree under the old unconditional prompt, and it committed (89b23e3d); every wave-2 candidate was cut from 'the wave-1 tip', which carried B1.1's work only because it committed. Under the new prompt that child is told its pack commits nothing. Decide whether document-tree should render the commit clause (it edits a git tree with isolation 'none'), or whether the frame owns committing a document-tree child's bytes — and say which in the adapter table, so the next reader does not have to re-derive it.

The prompt every child receives calls .orch-notes/ 'the reserved scratch directory the join never grades' in the same breath as telling each code-pack child to commit inside its candidate, so a child running git add -A re-commits it — which is what four children did.

findings.remedy: Add .orch-notes/ to .gitignore. One line, and it retires the integrator's manual sweep permanently.

findings.summary: The integrator's re-pin is sound in substance — net stronger, not weakened — but it re-pins an owner file's prose including its line wrap, which the code pack's own craft forbids. The same wording edit will break it again.
findings.evidence: 645256db replaces one assertion with two in tests/test_verification_model.py:68: assertIn("Write the complete\nseven-field findings array to one JSON file") becomes assertIn("Write the findings to one\nJSON file") plus assertIn("print `findings: <path>` in the report"). Net +1 assertion, so no check was weakened to reach green. But packs/orch-code-pack/references/craft.md's Shape section states: 'Checks pin shapes, never sentences: assert a field, a set, a count by kind, or a verdict — never an owner file's prose ... A check reading an owner file reads a stable anchor — a heading, a backticked name, a fenced command.' The new pin embeds a hard line break, so a pure re-wrap of that sentence in skills/kernel/orch-judge/SKILL.md — no semantic change at all — fails the test.
findings.cause: The integrator followed the surrounding idiom, which is the right instinct: every neighbouring assertion in CritiqueContractTest pins prose the same way. The frame's own wave-2 record named the symptom ('content-pack units touching test-pinned prose need a test-lane check or a code-pack stamp') but not this cause, which is that the pin reads prose rather than an anchor. Fixing the stamp does not stop the next wording edit from breaking the pin; fixing the pin does.
findings.remedy: Successor scope, not this run's: retarget CritiqueContractTest's assertions at anchors the craft allows — the backticked `findings: <path>` form and the fenced/backticked names — and drop the wrapped-prose fragments. Then a content-pack unit editing that body cannot break it by re-wrapping.

findings.summary: Two super-research adapters still emit the output timestamp through their own upstream constant, whose value coincidentally equals schema.INSTANT_FORMAT. The spec's carve-out covers parsing upstream grammars, not emitting the output convention through them.
findings.evidence: .orchflows/skills/super-research/scripts/super_research/schema.py:22 INSTANT_FORMAT = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ". adapters/_support/github_rest_records.py:47 ROUTE_INSTANT_FORMAT = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ" — same value, independently spelled — and :93 return moment.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc).strftime(ROUTE_INSTANT_FORMAT) is an emission path, not a parse. adapters/_support/stocktwits_records.py:46 and :95 are the identical shape. Every other adapter now reads RECORD_INSTANT_FORMAT = schema.INSTANT_FORMAT (bluesky_extract:54, hacker_news_config:226, open_page_document:77, prediction_markets_config:336, reddit_shreddit_contract:150, scholarly_records:19, and the 24-site sweep the driver recorded).
findings.cause: The spec ruled 'Distinct upstream wire-format grammars (X's, RFC 3339) keep their own constants; only the one output convention consolidates.' GitHub REST and StockTwits both speak RFC 3339 with Z, so their route constants are covered by the ruling for parsing — and the emission calls happen to reuse the same constant, which the ruling does not reach. This is the coinciding-values hazard the spec's own ruling 3 was written about, one level down.
findings.remedy: Two lines: have those two emission calls strftime through schema.INSTANT_FORMAT while their parse calls keep ROUTE_INSTANT_FORMAT. U12's stated acceptance ('the protocol.md claim is true by grep') holds on the claim's own words — references/protocol.md:103 says schema.INSTANT_FORMAT is the one definition and ordering reads it from there, and ordering.py:49 does — so this is reported, not repaired.
